text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [P1] Latency alert: router edge-allocator p99 spike > 3s in us-west-2 — paging oncall (emma)

emma (oncall): on it. linking dashboards? which routes affected?

raj (sre): p95 jumped from ~220ms -> ~620ms over last 8m, p99 from ~900ms -> 3.8s. streaming sessions show stalls (long tail) specifically on streaming route /v1/stream and some generate endpoints. dashboard: https://dash.company/reports/edge-allocator/17685

lia (router-eng): seeing routing policy rotation at 2026-03-15T06:12:03Z — weight shuffle for allocator groups. traffic skewed: ~27% of flows ended up on allocator shard rotor-7 (expected ~4-6%). logs indicate flow affinity mapping flapped during rollout.

tom (runtime): KV cache thrash on rotor-7, leading to continuous misses -> larger decode times + batching blowup. heap churn + backpressure to streaming workers. grabbing logs now.

nisha (ops): any customer impact? support?

olivia (support): noticing increased PSRs from a few customers in US-W region; one enterprise (acme-inc) reported repeated streaming pauses ~30-90s; they say some requests retried by client. open ticket #C-9921.

emma (oncall): immediate mitigations idea list: 1) revert routing-policy rollout to previous stable 2) temporarily scale allocator pool to spread load 3) hot-shard eviction/rebalance. which is fastest?

lia (router-eng): fastest is to pin routing-policy back to v2.2.9 (rollback). also we can mark rotor-7 as drained (manual exclude) to rebalance. I can push rollback now.

raj (sre): scaling buys time but won't fix misrouting. if we drain rotor-7 we should see p99 come down quickly. recommend rollback + drain.

lia (router-eng): executing rollback -> applying policy v2.2.9 now.

deploy-bot: @lia initiated rollback of routing-policy service at 06:17:14Z: v2.3.1 -> v2.2.9. CI checks passed.

lia (router-eng): draining rotor-7: setting allocator label evict:true and triggering rebalance.

emma (oncall): commands for ops if needed (copy):
```
# scale allocators
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/edge-allocator --replicas=12
# mark shard for drain
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" https://controlplane/api/allocators/rotor-7/drain
```

nisha (ops): scaling to 12 replicas now.

tom (runtime): observing KV cache miss rate drop on rotor-7 after drain start. batching latency per-invocation down ~30% on that node.

raj (sre): p95 now 280ms, p99 trending down 1.4s -> 920ms over last 2m. good sign.

olivia (support): told acme-inc support that we're investigating and applied mitigations; asking for logs if they can reproduce.

emma (oncall): assigning follow-ups: @lia to write short postmortem draft, @tom to validate cache eviction heuristics and add a synthetic test for allocator skew, @raj to add alert guarding >10% shard weight shift within 5m.

lia (router-eng): noted root cause hypothesis: policy rotation algorithm allowed transient weight drift when allocation target counts are low for certain flow keys. rotation-induced herd to single shard (rotor-7) amplified by small lag in affinity update propagation. will add stricter sanity checks.

tom (runtime): runtime-level patch candidates: pre-check to limit continuous batching window if KV miss rate spikes > X; also guard against prolonged high-batch-size on single node. I'll open PR with benchmark.

raj (sre): quick numbers for incident log: peak p99 3.8s at 06:16Z, impacted fraction ~1.6% of total requests in us-west-2 during window 06:12–06:20Z, streaming sessions with stalls ~0.08% but customer-visible.

olivia (support): acme-inc will accept postmortem and request confirmation of rollback + monitoring.

lia (router-eng): post-rollback checks: router weights converged back to expected distribution within 45s after rollback. rotor-7 traffic <6% now.

deploy-bot: rollback completed and healthy >5m.

emma (oncall): closing the live page at 06:22Z — monitoring for 30m. creating incident thread to incidents-triage for full writeup. thanks all. :raised_hands:

raj (sre): follow-up items (ticket numbers): SRE-458 (alert), RTE-102 (runtime guard), ROUTE-88 (rotation algorithm tests).

lia (router-eng): will schedule canary re-roll with staged weight checks and rollout gating.

nisha (ops): leaving scaling at 12 for cool-down for next 15m then ramp to steady state.

olivia (support): tagging acme-inc ticket with rollback and ETA for postmortem.

emma (oncall): final note: impact small but customer-visible; mitigation quick due to rollback + drain. postmortem to include timeline + planned code and alerting changes.

incident-bot: Incident closed to live paging at 06:22:50Z, severity downgraded to SEV2 for documentation.
